conviction_note: Q3 is close to pre-released: the QuantumCell USD 7m licence revenue and all USD 22m of upfronts received in August were announced, so the reported quarter carries almost nothing new. What is new is the acting CEO's first letter (after an unexplained 'mutual agreement' CEO exit on 27 Oct) and any wording on pain-project partnering. I found nothing unpriced, so p_up is 48: a faint lean from three of the last four report days closing down and a +7.8% five-day run-up into the print. abs_move is 4.5 because turnover is thin. The findings sum to 0.0 and the scaled number is -0.18; both say there is no edge, so the small gap means nothing.

H1 report: cash SEK 13.5m at 30 June. The SEK 30.1m rights issue had not yet been recognised in the group. CEO letter says 'during August alone we received upfront payments totaling USD 22 million'. CEO Martin Jönsson leaves by mutual agreement; co-founder and CSO Johan Sandin becomes acting CEO and Pontus Forsell deputy CEO. The stated focus going forward is the Lilly and QuantumCell collaborations plus the Painless pain platform
Redeye fair value SEK 13 per share, set in its Q2 review. The stock rose +22.3% that day (27 Aug), the day after the report

Any update on the pain-project partnering talks the H1 report and the September CEO interview disclosed. Probably a reiteration; a deal would come as separate inside information, not in the report
None. The company gives no financial guidance, only 'in line with plan' wording

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue and cash lines are effectively pre-released. The USD 7m QuantumCell licence payment (about SEK 66m of Q3 net sales) and USD 22m of total upfronts were received and announced in August, so a 'profit and SEK ~200m cash' quarter is arithmetic the market already has.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 had the first-ever revenue (SEK 97m, already known from the Lilly deal) and the stock fell -1.9% on the report day (26 Aug), then rose +22.3% the next day on Redeye's SEK 13 fair-value note. Observed report-day closes: Q3'25 +2.3%, Q4'25 -6.2%, Q1'26 -1.1%, Q2'26 -1.9% (Yahoo daily bars, report dates from the Nasdaq Nordic feed)
findings.original_quote: bara under augusti har vi erhållit upfrontbetalningar om totalt 22 miljoner USD (H1 report CEO letter, Swedish version: 'in August alone we have received upfront payments totalling USD 22 million')
findings.why_not_priced: It IS priced: every component was published in August. If the market had NOT priced it, the stock would sit near the pre-deal cash-adjusted level. Instead it trades at about SEK 980m market cap, roughly 4-5x the computable cash, and has held SEK 6-8 since the deals. Sized at 0 because the market has already been told the number.
findings.independence: Same fact in the Swedish H1 release https://mfn.se/a/alzecure-pharma/alzecure-offentliggor-delarsrapport-for-januari-juni-2026 (same issuer, not independent)

findings.finding: The CEO left 'by mutual agreement' on 27 Oct, two weeks before this report and with no reason given beyond a 'new phase'. The Q3 report is the first under acting CEO and co-founder Johan Sandin, so its letter is the first chance for anything behind the exit (strategy shift, cost reset, severance) to surface.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO change in the sample. The stock rose +3.2% on 27 Oct (the release came at 18:30, after the close) and +0.9% on 28 Oct, then drifted from 6.52 to 6.02 by 5 Nov before recovering to 6.64 at the seal
findings.original_quote: Styrelsen och Martin Jönsson, VD i AlzeCure Pharma sedan januari 2020, har enats om att han nu lämnar sin befattning. ('The Board and Martin Jönsson, CEO of AlzeCure Pharma since January 2020, have agreed that he now leaves his position.')
findings.why_not_priced: The change itself is priced: it was public on 27 Oct and Redeye commented on 28 Oct without new numbers. What is not priced is the content of the acting CEO's first report, which nobody has seen. Its sign is unknown, so it is sized near zero with a wide range. A market that already priced a bad reason would show a sharp drop on 28 Oct; instead the stock rose that day.
findings.independence: Redeye's note comments on the change without numbers: https://borsvarlden.com/finwire/CRF00F9B92 (same event)

findings.finding: Partnering talks on the pain projects are live by the company's own account. The H1 report says discussions are underway with other parties, and the CEO said in September that external parties had proposed deals for ACD440, some wanting to finance and drive it. The Q3 report may sharpen that wording.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two signed out-licensing deals moved the stock +246.6% (9 Jun, Lilly) and +60.2% (1 Jul, QuantumCell), but both came as separate inside-information releases at 07:00-07:10, not inside a periodic report. Report-day wording on talks has not moved it before
findings.original_quote: Discussions are underway with other parties regarding the company's pain projects. Swedish-press corroboration: Placera telegram 2026-09-07 'Ökade aktiviteter Painless efter partneravtal - VD' (https://www.placera.se/telegram/alzecure-pharma-okade-aktiviteter-painless-efter-partneravtal-vd-20260907; reached only through a WebFetch summary, verbatim Swedish text not retrieved)
findings.why_not_priced: The talks were disclosed in August and September, so their existence is priced. Only an escalation in wording inside the report would be new, and a signed deal would come as a separate MAR release, probably not on report day. Hence a small positive size: the probability of escalation in the window is low.
findings.independence: Placera/Finwire CEO interview 2026-09-07 https://www.placera.se/telegram/alzecure-pharma-okade-aktiviteter-painless-efter-partneravtal-vd-20260907 (a different outlet, but the same speaker)

outside_window.finding: Redeye's post-report review has come one to three days after the report (Q3'25 review on 2025-11-14; the Q2'26 review on 27 Aug moved the stock +22.3% on a SEK 13 fair value against a 6.64 spot). A Q3 review would land after the 11 Nov close.
